formulations.label: Chewable tablets 4 mmol
formulations.strengths: Magnesium glycerophosphate equivalent to 4 mmol (97.2 mg) magnesium per tablet
formulations.note: Contains aspartame (10 mg per tablet) and phosphate. The score line is for ease of swallowing, not for dividing into equal doses.

src.q: Each chewable tablet contains magnesium glycerophosphate equivalent to 4 mmol (97.2 mg) of magnesium.
Each tablet contains 10 mg aspartame.
The score line is only to facilitate breaking for ease of swallowing and not to divide into equal doses.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Chronic magnesium loss or hypomagnesaemia diagnosed by a doctor.

src.q: indicated as oral magnesium supplements for the treatment of patients with chronic magnesium loss or hypomagnesaemia as diagnosed by a doctor

items.t: Adults with hypomagnesaemia caused by loop or thiazide diuretics or other drugs that cause hypomagnesaemia.

src.q: also indicated for adult patients with hypomagnesaemia due to the concomitant administration of loop and thiazide diuretics or other drugs which cause hypomagnesaemia

items.t: Children: use only if benefits outweigh risks and under supervision of physicians experienced in managing hypomagnesaemia in children.

src.q: Neomag tablets should only be used if the benefits of treatment outweigh any potential risks and under the supervision of physicians experienced in the management of children with hypomagnesaemia.

items.t: Severe symptomatic hypomagnesaemia: give IV magnesium first to restore levels, before oral magnesium glycerophosphate.

src.q: Patients with severe, symptomatic hypomagnesaemia should receive intravenous magnesium repletion for acute recovery of magnesium levels prior to receiving Neomag.

items.t: Adults (over 18 years): start 4-8 mmol (1-2 tablets) three times a day (12-24 mmol/day in divided doses); adjust to serum total magnesium. Elderly: no dose adjustment.

src.q: Starting doses for adult patients are recommended as 4-8 mmol (1-2 tablets) administered 3 times a day.
This equates to a total dose of 12 to 24 mmol per day taken in divided doses.
Elderly: No dose adjustment is necessary.

items.t: SPS (mild hypomagnesaemia, 0.5-0.7 mmol/L): total daily oral dose 10-24 mmol magnesium in divided doses. Commonly given for up to 7 days, then recheck serum magnesium; continue 1-2 days after levels normalise.
items.tag: SPS: mild acute hypomagnesaemia in adults

src.q: Give a total daily oral dose of 10 to 24mmol of magnesium in divided doses.
It is common practice to prescribe oral magnesium replacement for up to 7 days and then repeat the serum magnesium level.
Continue treatment for 1 to 2 days after magnesium levels normalise.

items.t: Start low (e.g. 1 tablet per dose) and increase gradually to the maximum tolerated dose.

src.q: Start with a low dose, such as 1 tablet per dose, and gradually increase to a maximum tolerated dose.

items.t: Under 4 years: not recommended (insufficient information).

src.q: Children: below 4 years : Not recommended as there is insufficient information regarding the use of Neomag tablets in this age group.

items.t: 4 to 12 years: start 4 mmol (1 tablet) twice a day (8 mmol/day); adjust to serum total magnesium.

src.q: A starting dose for children 4 to 12 years is recommended as 4 mmol (1 tablet) administered 2 times a day.
This equates to a total dose of 8 mmol per day taken in divided doses.

items.t: 12 to 18 years: start 4 mmol (1 tablet) three times a day (12 mmol/day); adjust to serum total magnesium.

src.q: A starting dose for children 12 to 18 years is recommended as 4 mmol (1 tablet) administered 3 times a day.
This equates to a total dose of 12 mmol per day taken in divided doses.

items.t: Use only under supervision of physicians experienced in childhood hypomagnesaemia; monitor serum magnesium regularly.

src.q: under the supervision of physicians experienced in the management of children with hypomagnesaemia

items.t: Hypersensitivity to magnesium glycerophosphate or any excipient.

src.q: Do not administer Neomag tablets if there is evidence of hypersensitivity to the active substance

items.t: Severe renal impairment (glomerular filtration rate < 30 ml/min).

src.q: Neomag is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment (glomerularfiltration rate < 30 ml/min).

items.t: Should not be given in phenylketonuria (contains aspartame) or hyperphosphataemia (contains phosphate). Both are listed in SmPC 4.3.

src.q: Neomag should not be administered to patients with phenylketonuria as Neomag tablets contain Aspartame.
Neomag should not be administered to patients with hyperphosphataemia as Neomag tablets contain phosphate.

items.t: Absorption may be reduced after extensive bowel resection.

src.q: in patients who have undergone extensive bowel resection the absorption of magnesium may be reduced

items.t: Look for and correct hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia, which often occur with magnesium deficiency.

src.q: concomitant hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia should be suspected and corrected if confirmed

items.t: Hypermagnesaemia is possible with higher doses and impaired renal function.

src.q: Hypermagnesaemia is possible with higher doses and with impaired renal function.

items.t: Magnesium and other medicines can affect each other's absorption: generally keep 2 to 3 hours apart where possible.

src.q: As magnesium and other medicinal products may mutually influence each other's absorption, a time interval of 2 to 3 hours should generally be respected if possible.

items.t: Iron, aminoquinolines (e.g. hydroxychloroquine), quinidine, nitrofurantoin, penicillamine, bisphosphonates, eltrombopag, nitroxoline: take magnesium 3 to 4 hours before or after these.

src.q: Aminoquinolines, quinidine and quinidine derivatives, nitrofurantoin, penicillamine, iron, bisphosphonates (such as alendronate and risedronate), eltrombopag, nitroxoline
magnesium preparations should be taken 3 to 4 hours before or after the administration of those drugs

items.t: Ciprofloxacin SmPC: give ciprofloxacin 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after magnesium-containing products.

src.q: multivalent cation-containing drugs and mineral supplements (e.g. calcium, magnesium, aluminium, iron)
ciprofloxacin should be administered either 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after these preparations

items.t: Proton pump inhibitors (e.g. omeprazole), thiazide and loop diuretics, aminoglycosides, cisplatin, ciclosporin and others increase magnesium loss: the magnesium dose may need adjusting.

src.q: Because of increased magnesium losses, a dose adjustment of magnesium may be necessary when taking the following substances
proton pump inhibitors (such as omeprazole and pantoprazole)

items.t: Tetracyclines and fluorides: separate doses by 2 to 3 hours or more.

src.q: Fluorides and tetracycline : if they must be used, the doses must be separated by 2 to 3 hours or more

items.t: Digoxin: magnesium deficiency may enhance digoxin toxicity.

src.q: Magnesium deficiency may enhance digoxin toxicity.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated if glomerular filtration rate < 30 ml/min. No dose adjustment in mild to moderate renal impairment.

src.q: Neomag is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment (glomerularfiltration rate < 30 ml/min).
There is no dose adjustment necessary in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment.

items.t: SPS: seek specialist advice before magnesium replacement in severe kidney disease (CKD 4 or 5), acute kidney injury, dialysis or kidney transplant. No oral dose adjustment needed in CKD 1 to 3.

src.q: Seek specialist advice before prescribing magnesium replacement to patients with the following: severe kidney disease (CKD 4 or 5) acute kidney injury receiving dialysis a kidney transplant
No dose adjustments are needed for oral magnesium replacement.

items.t: SPS (general, all routes): lower doses may be required in renal impairment because of the risk of hypermagnesaemia.

src.q: Lower doses may be required in renal impairment due to the risk of hypermagnesaemia.

items.t: Monitor serum magnesium regularly, especially in renal impairment.

src.q: particularly in children and in patients with renal impairment

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment advice in the magnesium glycerophosphate SmPC or the SPS hypomagnesaemia page.

items.t: Safety not established in pregnancy: use only if benefits outweigh risks. Long-term data from pre-eclampsia treatment do not suggest malformative or fetal/neonatal toxicity of magnesium.

src.q: Neomag tablets should only be used in pregnancy if the benefits of the treatment outweigh any potential risks.
long-term data available from treatment of pre-eclampsia do not indicate malformative or feto/neonatal toxicity of magnesium

items.t: Can be used during breastfeeding; passes into milk but no effects on the infant are expected at therapeutic doses.

src.q: Neomag can be used during breast-feeding.
at therapeutic doses of Neomag no effects on the breastfed newborns/infants are anticipated

items.t: No effects on male or female fertility are expected.

src.q: no effects of magnesium on male and female fertility are anticipated

items.t: Diarrhoea, usually dose dependent: reduce the daily dose, then increase gradually if needed. Frequency not stated.

src.q: Neomag may cause diarrhoea, which is usually dose dependent.
If diarrhoea occurs, the daily dose should be reduced and gradually increased later if needed.

items.t: Hypermagnesaemia (flushing, thirst, low blood pressure, drowsiness, confusion, loss of tendon reflexes, muscle weakness, respiratory depression, arrhythmias): stop magnesium; IV calcium gluconate in severe toxicity.

src.q: Hypermagnesaemia characterised by flushing, thirst, hypotension, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, confusion, loss of tendon reflexes due to neuromuscular blockade, muscle weakness, respiratory depression, cardiac arrhythmias, coma and cardiac arrest.
When hypermagnesaemia is found, magnesium therapy should be withdrawn

items.t: Persistent diarrhoea or symptoms: IV replacement may be needed (SPS).

src.q: If diarrhoea persists or the patient becomes symptomatic, IV magnesium replacement may be necessary.

items.t: Before and during treatment: adjust the dose to the serum total magnesium level; look for and correct hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia.

src.q: The dosage regimen should be adjusted according to the serum total magnesium level of the individual patient.
concomitant hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia should be suspected and corrected if confirmed

items.t: SmPC: monitor serum magnesium at regular intervals (e.g. every 3-6 months), especially in children and renal impairment.

src.q: It is recommended that serum magnesium levels should be monitored at regular intervals (e.g. every 3-6 months)

items.t: SPS: repeat serum magnesium 7 days after starting oral therapy and again after 1 to 3 months; also monitor serum calcium, potassium and renal function.

src.q: Repeat the serum magnesium level 7 days after starting oral therapy and again after 1 to 3 months
serum calcium and potassium renal function

items.t: If hypermagnesaemia develops, withdraw magnesium.

src.q: When hypermagnesaemia is found, magnesium therapy should be withdrawn

items.t: Tablets may be broken into quarters and chewed or swallowed with water.

src.q: The tablet may be broken into quarters and chewed or swallowed with water.

items.t: SPS: take with meals and in divided doses.

src.q: Advise patients to take oral magnesium with meals and in divided doses.

items.t: May cause diarrhoea; tell the prescriber if it happens (dose can be reduced).

src.q: If diarrhoea occurs, the daily dose should be reduced and gradually increased later if needed.

src.q: Neomag should not be administered to patients with phenylketonuria as Neomag tablets contain Aspartame.
